_doc: Single source of truth. v = value; src = URL (sourced) or est = reasoning (estimate). Namespaces: vehicle.*, pad.*, physics.*, scene.*. Merged from research/*.spec.json; conflicts resolved by the orchestrator (see research/notes.md).

vehicle.booster.propellant_mass.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship (Block 3; Wikipedia Super Heavy page says 3400 t for earlier blocks)

vehicle.booster.engine_ring_outer.radius.est: Outer ring pitch radius; nozzle edge at 4.55 m, flush with the 4.5 m skirt (the engine shields slightly flare). Orchestrator decision.

vehicle.booster.engine_ring_mid.radius.est: 10 x 1.2 m nozzles need at least 1.91 m; 2.45 leaves a 0.3 m gap to the outer ring

vehicle.booster.engine_ring_centre.radiu.est: 3 engines mutually 108-108-144 deg per NSF/search summary https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/

vehicle.booster.engine_ring_mid.clock_of.est: mid ring rotated for pad deflector; amount unknown; 18 deg would be half pitch of 36 deg, 9 deg chosen as placeholder

vehicle.raptor3.nozzle_exit_diameter_sl.est: Packing constraint: 20 outer nozzles must fit on a ring inside the 4.5 m skirt radius (2*pi*3.95/20 = 1.24 m spacing). Raptor 1's 1.3 m would overlap. Orchestrator decision.

vehicle.raptor3.length_sl.est: Raptor 2 sea-level ~3.1 m; Raptor 3 slightly shorter

vehicle.raptor3.rvac_nozzle_exit_diamete.est: RVac about 2.4 m per general knowledge; not confirmed by search

vehicle.booster.engine_plane_y.est: reference origin: nozzle exit plane; thrust plate about 3.2 m above

vehicle.booster.engine_thrust_plate_heig.est: aft skirt with four 1.4 m rings starts about 3-5 m up; V3 engines mounted on steel plate not dome (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/)

vehicle.booster.common_dome_height.est: fits photo frost boundary at y=366 px => 45 m up; propellant split about 78/22 by mass (O/F 3.6) gives about 57/43 by volume

vehicle.booster.hot_stage_zone.bottom_he.est: integrated open N1-style truss hot-stage, exhaust hits booster forward dome (https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/05/super-heavy-block-3-booster-future/)

vehicle.booster.hot_stage_zone.height.est: 72.3 minus 62; vented open truss with about 12 struts

vehicle.booster.hot_stage_vent_count.est: Placeholder for the vent bays in the integrated open truss; the real count is not published.

vehicle.booster.grid_fin.count.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy (Block 3: three grid fins, roughly 1.5 times the size of the Block 1 and 2 fins, integrated with the catch pins)

vehicle.booster.grid_fin.scale_vs_v2.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy (Block 3: three grid fins, roughly 1.5 times the size of the Block 1 and 2 fins, integrated with the catch pins)

vehicle.booster.grid_fin.azimuth_deg.est: Photo: fins protrude on both silhouette sides with the belly at azimuth 90; supersedes [0,120,240]

vehicle.booster.grid_fin.hinge_height.est: Photo-derived by the vehicle builder: fins are visible as horizontal dashes about 5.5 m below the ship base (rows about 331). Supersedes the research estimate of 62.5 m.

vehicle.booster.grid_fin.span.est: V2 fin about 2.9 x 3.3 m scaled to give 1.5x area (ratio 1.22 each side)

vehicle.booster.catch_pin_count.est: two pins on opposite sides for chopsticks

vehicle.booster.catch_pin_height.est: Estimated near the top of the booster in the hot-stage region, about 64 m up; the position is not published (Pad 2 chopsticks are about 10 m shorter than Pad 1: https://nasaspaceflight.com/2025/08/starbase-pad-2-advancements-pad-1/).

vehicle.booster.raceway_count.est: cable raceways run along the booster length

vehicle.ship.length.est: 124 m stack (src SFN) minus 72.3 m booster = 51.7; V2 ship 52.1 m (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship_(spacecraft)). Wikipedia lists Block 3 ship as 61 m (est) which contradicts the 124 m stack; rejected

vehicle.ship.rvac.radius.est: centre triangle of 3 RVac with 2.4 m nozzles; spacing 2.9 m

vehicle.ship.rsl.radius.est: 3 sea-level engines in outer ring, clocked 60 deg from RVacs

vehicle.ship.aft_flap.hinge_height.est: side of engine bay/LOX tank; V2 aft flap about 9 x 4 m

vehicle.ship.aft_flap.size.est: length x chord; photo flare 26 px wide about 15.5 m

vehicle.ship.forward_flap.hinge_height.est: just below nose cone base; V2/V3 thinner, angled about 140 deg (src W3 for angle)

vehicle.ship.nose.height.est: tangent ogive; tip radius about 0.3 m; header tanks in nose

vehicle.ship.nose.tip_radius.est: photo tip 5 px wide about 3 m at blur; real tip smaller

vehicle.ship.nose.profile.v: power-law cone r = R (x/L)^0.85, blunt tip 0.3 m, blended over the last 2.4 m
vehicle.ship.nose.profile.est: Photo nose is slimmer than a tangent ogive (about 6.8 m wide 7.6 m below the tip)

vehicle.ship.common_dome_height.est: LOX below, CH4 above; O/F 3.6 gives about 58% of tank volume LOX

vehicle.ship.header_tank_height.est: LOX and CH4 header tanks in the nose; V2 had them inside the nose cone/payload bay

vehicle.ship.tile.hex_size.est: Hexagon across flats about 30-35 cm (one source says about 20 cm per side, i.e. about 35 cm across flats); no official figure found.

vehicle.ship.tile.gap.est: About 5-6 mm expansion gap, an estimate; the fact that gaps exist to allow heat expansion is from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship_(spacecraft)

vehicle.ship.tile.coverage.est: photo: ship looks black over full visible length

vehicle.ship.leeward.colour.est: not visible in photo; 304L tumbled finish

vehicle.ship.qd_plate.height.est: ship quick-disconnect / QD plate near forward end of the tank section; Block 3 adds refuelling hardware (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starship)

vehicle.stack.hot_stage_gap.est: ship engine bells nested in booster hot-stage truss at liftoff

vehicle.photo.frost_boundary_height.est: Read off the reference photo: frost boundary at image row 366, engine plane at row 441, about 0.61 m per pixel gives (441-366) x 0.61 = 46 m, rounded to 45 m. The pixel scale is approximate, and the boundary is where the frost changes brightness, not a measured tank position.

pad.frame.v: origin = Pad 2 (OLP-2) vehicle axis at ground level; x east, y up, z south
pad.frame.est: Origin lat 25.99680, lon -97.15804 derived from OSM (centre of the gap between Pad 2 chopstick arm ways). Cross-check: Launch Library alias OLP-2 = 25.99677,-97.15799 https://www.spacelaunchschedule.com/pad/orbital-launch-pad-2-spacex-starbase-tx-usa/ (about 4 m away).

pad.ground_elevation_asl.src: OSM tag ele=2.5 on way 1207227015 Starbase Integration Tower 2

pad.pad_id.est: Photo geometry (tower north of vehicle, camera looks NNE, OSM overlay aligns) plus Flight 14 launched from OLP-2 https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship_flight_14

pad.flight_id.est: Wikipedia flight 14. Photo light comes from the right/rear (sun ESE) = morning; flights 12/13 launched 17:30-17:51 CDT with sun in the west, so they are unlikely. Photo posted 22:30 on 2026-09-28 fits.

pad.tower2_centre.src: OSM way 1207227015 footprint centre in local frame

pad.tower2_footprint.est: OSM footprint bbox 16x16 (way 1207227015); photo shows lattice body only ~12-13 m wide aloft, so 16 m probably includes rails/legs

pad.tower2_body_width_photo.est: 18-20 px wide at ~1.53 px/m in reference.jpeg

pad.tower2_height.src: OSM height=144.5 citing FAA OE case 619969843; Fandom OLIT-3 '474 ft (144.5 m)' https://starship-spacex.fandom.com/wiki/Orbital_Launch_and_Integration_Tower_3_(OLIT-3)

pad.tower_height_range_faa.src: FAA structural filings list OLIT units 469-479 ft incl. lightning masts (Fandom OLIT page https://starship-spacex.fandom.com/wiki/Orbital_Launch_and_Integration_Tower_(OLIT)); Wikipedia says 146 m https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Starbase. Conflict: 144.5 (pad 2) vs 143 (pad 1, OSM) vs 146 (Wikipedia); chosen 144.5 for pad 2.

pad.tower_offset_from_axis.est: from OSM tower centre (-3,-27) to axis (0,0); tower is NORTH of the vehicle

pad.chopstick_side.v: south (+z) of tower face, i.e. towards the OLM
pad.chopstick_side.est: OSM gantry ways 1540152640-52 extend from tower face z=-19 to z=+8

pad.chopstick_reach_from_tower_face.src: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1540152640 (OSM gantry ways 1540152640-52: carriage z -17..-8, arms z -8..+8; crowd-mapped, +-3 m)

pad.chopstick_arm_length.est: OSM arm ways ~16 m plus hinge; Pad B arms are 'noticeably shorter' than Pad A: https://spaceexplored.com/2025/07/28/the-key-differences-between-starships-pad-a-and-b/ ; https://www.teslaoracle.com/2025/03/25/spacex-installs-redesigned-chopsticks-pad-b-launch-tower-starship-catch-giga-bay-construction-starbase-updates/

pad.chopstick_inner_gap_closed_x.est: OSM arm inner edges: 12 m gap for the 9 m booster; arm axis x=+1 before origin shift

pad.chopstick_carriage_height_in_photo.est: crossbar with fork ends at image y~495; tower base row ~685; 1.53 px/m; +-6 m

pad.chopstick_open_span_photo.est: crossbar 782->852 px at 1.53 px/m (arms swung open)

pad.qd_arm_boom_height_in_photo.est: boom with hanging line on west side of tower at image y~585; probable QD/service arm; LOW confidence

pad.pad2_booster_QDs.v: dual booster quick disconnects (LCH4 and LOX) on the opposite side of the mount from Pad 1

pad.lightning_masts.v: on tower top; included in the 143-146 m FAA height

pad.olm_height.est: LOW confidence recollection of OLM table height; NSF forum thread 'OLM height and width' https://forum.nasaspaceflight.com/index.php?topic=58105.0 could not be fetched (403)

pad.olm_shape_pad2.v: square/'quadratic' water-cooled deck with central circular booster opening; 20 hold-down clamp arms; rolled to Pad B 6 May 2025, lifted onto columns 12 May 2025

pad.olm_footprint_pad2.est: LOW confidence, unsourced: about 34 x 34 m from the chopstick width plus support columns.

pad.flame_trench_pad2.v: dedicated bathtub-shaped sheet-pile/CFA-pile reinforced-concrete trench, stainless-lined, water-cooled double-sided flame-bucket diverter beneath the mount

pad.flame_trench_pad2_orientation.v: long axis east-west; exhaust splits east and west
pad.flame_trench_pad2_orientation.est: photo: cloud banks left/right, none towards camera; tower north, arms south

pad.flame_trench_pad2_size.est: LOW confidence, no published dimensions: 60 x 25 x 8 m (length, width, depth). OpenStreetMap maps the trench polygon at about 84 x 18 m (way tagged construction:aeroway=flame_trench).

pad.pad1_axis.est: OSM tower1 centre (331.5,74.5), arms z 62..82 and x to 368 -> axis 19 m from tower face, same rule as pad 2

pad.pad1_status.v: decommissioned 14 Oct 2025 for V3 upgrades (11 launches, 3 booster catches); under reconstruction in 2026

pad.pad1_mount_shape.v: original circular donut mount with water-cooled steel deluge plate, no flame trench
pad.pad1_mount_shape.src: https://spaceexplored.com/2025/07/28/the-key-differences-between-starships-pad-a-and-b/ ; OSM shows a 'Flame Trench' polygon at pad 1 (67x77 m centre (366,74), way 1549519359)

pad.tank_farm_extent.src: OSM way 'SpaceX Orbital Launch Pad Tank Farm'

pad.tank_farm_pad2_end_centre.src: OSM 'Pad 2 LOX GSE' 58x42 m; 'Pad 2 CH4 GSE' centre (182,-59) 64x35 m

pad.tank_horizontal_lox_ln2.src: OSM storage_tank rectangles, LOX/LN2, centres x 219..352, z -52..-29, long axis ~12.5 deg off east-west

pad.tank_horizontal_ch4_large.src: OSM storage_tank ways at x 358..394, z -26..-21

pad.tank_water_deluge.src: OSM storage_tank content=water at x 52..98, z -72..-60 (nearest Pad 2)

pad.vaporizers.src: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1290585485 (22 ways named Vaporizer in the OpenStreetMap extract, e.g. ways 1290585485-1290585487; crowd-mapped)

pad.coast_distance_east.src: OSM natural=coastline ways 1230230739/975/976 at x~+750 near pad latitude

pad.coast_bearing.v: NNW-SSE, about 6 deg east of south going south

physics.ship_height_m.est: stack minus booster; SFN F14 says 52 m https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/09/21/spacexs-super-heavy-booster-arrives-at-pad-ahead-of-first-orbital-starship-launch/ ; W-SS table lists 61 m (rejected)

physics.booster_dry_mass_b3_t.est: not published; assume near Block 2 275 t, +10 t

physics.ship_dry_mass_b3_t.est: not found; Block 2 = 85 t (W-SS), V3 heavier, range 100-130

physics.payload_mass_f14_t.est: 26 Starlink V3 sats x ~1.7 t (F13: 20 sats = 34.1 t, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship_flight_test_13)

physics.liftoff_mass_published_t.src: https://newspaceeconomy.ca/2026/04/16/detailed-review-of-starship-v3/ ("gross liftoff mass in the vicinity of 5,300 tons"; one secondary review, which also assumes a 3,400 t booster load, so not an official SpaceX figure)

physics.liftoff_mass_sum_of_parts_t.est: 285 (booster dry, est) + 3650 + 120 (ship dry, est) + 1600 + 44 (payload, est) = 5,700 t. Conflicts with the 5,300 t of one review; the dry masses are unpublished estimates.

physics.liftoff_mass_used_t.est: Midpoint chosen for the model; plausible range 5,300-5,700 t (T/W 1.55 down to 1.45, freeze time 7.0-7.8 s). The true figure is not published.

physics.liftoff_thrust_b3_MN.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy (Block 3 max thrust 80.8 MN = 33 x 250 tf). One Flight 14 news report says "some 16 million pounds" in total; see physics.liftoff_thrust_f14_report_Mlbf

physics.liftoff_thrust_alt_280tf_MN.est: 33 x 280 tf x 9.80665; press claim in https://newspaceeconomy.ca/2026/04/16/detailed-review-of-starship-v3/ (rejected)

physics.liftoff_tw_central.est: 80.8e6 N / (5.4e6 kg x 9.80665 m/s2), from the used liftoff mass. Uncertain by about +-0.05.

physics.liftoff_tw_range_low.est: Same thrust with 5,700 t (sum of parts): 80.8e6 / (5.7e6 x 9.80665).

physics.liftoff_tw_range_high.est: Same thrust with 5,300 t (one review's figure): 80.8e6 / (5.3e6 x 9.80665).

physics.raptor_of_ratio.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Raptor (3.6 for Raptor 1 and 2; Raptor 3 assumed the same)

physics.raptor3_isp_sl_used_s.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy (Block 3 sea-level Isp); W-RAP Raptor 3 row says 350 (conflict)

physics.raptor3_isp_vac_s.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy (Block 3 booster engines: SL 330 s, Vac 350 s); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Raptor lists 350 s for sea level and 380 s vacuum target for Raptor 3, a conflict

physics.raptor_nozzle_exit_diameter_m.est: Assumed 1.2 m so that 20 outer nozzles fit inside the 9 m skirt (shared with vehicle.raptor3.nozzle_exit_diameter_sl). Raptor 3 nozzle size is not published; Raptor 1 is 1.3 m (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Raptor), and the sourced Isp ratio 350/330 would imply a somewhat larger exit area.

physics.raptor_nozzle_expansion_ratio.est: Raptor 1 sea-level value from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Raptor (34.34, 1.3 m nozzle). The Raptor 3 value is not published; assumed the same.

physics.raptor_chamber_temperature_K.est: Estimate: adiabatic flame temperature of methane and oxygen near O/F 3.6 at high pressure (about 3,500-3,700 K). No published Raptor figure.

physics.raptor_exit_static_temperature_K.est: Isentropic expansion from 3,600 K at Mach 4.1 with gamma 1.2 gives about 1,340 K (1,050-1,700 K for gamma 1.15-1.25). Not measured.

physics.raptor_exit_pressure_bar.est: Isentropic estimate, gamma 1.2, chamber pressure 330 bar, expansion ratio 34 (Mach 4.1): p_exit = 330 bar x 0.00254 = 0.84 bar (0.7-1.0 for gamma 1.15-1.25 and Pc 300-350 bar). Not a published figure. Matches ambient pressure at about 1.6 km altitude.

physics.raptor_exhaust_velocity_sl_mps.est: Effective exhaust velocity at sea level = Isp x g0 = 330 s x 9.80665 m/s2 (Isp from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Super_Heavy).

physics.mdot_booster_total_kgps.est: Total mass flow = sea-level thrust / (Isp x g0) = 80.8 MN / (330 s x 9.80665). Calculated, not published; a 350 s Isp would give about 5 % less.

physics.mdot_lox_total_kgps.est: Total flow x 3.6/4.6 (oxidiser share at mixture ratio 3.6).

physics.mdot_ch4_total_kgps.est: Total flow x 1/4.6 (fuel share at mixture ratio 3.6).

physics.booster_full_thrust_burn_time_s.est: 3,650 t of propellant divided by the total flow of 25 t/s. Real cut-off comes earlier (about T+140 s) and real throttle settings are not published.

physics.jet_mechanical_power_GW.est: 0.5 x thrust x effective exhaust velocity = 0.5 x 80.8 MN x 3,236 m/s.

physics.chemical_power_GW.est: Methane flow 5.43 t/s x 50 MJ/kg lower heating value, assuming it all burns (part of it burns only after mixing with air).

physics.vac_thrust_booster_MN.est: Sea-level thrust plus p0 x exit area: 80.8 + 3.78 MN with 33 x 1.131 m2 (1.2 m nozzles). A 1.3 m nozzle would give 85.3 MN; the sourced Isp ratio 350/330 suggests about +6 %.

physics.thrust_gain_150m_pct.est: (p at deck 20 m - p at 158 m) x total exit area / thrust = about 1,700 Pa x 37.3 m2 / 80.8 MN = 0.08 %.

physics.engine_start_note.v: ignition T-3 s, ramp ~2.5-3 s, release at ~full thrust at T+0
physics.engine_start_note.est: W-SH gives only the 3 s lead

physics.tower_height_used_m.est: verified within +-2 m across sources; includes mast, measured from ground

physics.olm_height_m.est: No published figure found (searches and a fetch of the Fandom launch-mount page failed); 20 m is a recollection, plausible range 15-25 m. It sets the engine-plane start height and so the freeze time.

physics.base_rise_to_tower_top_m.est: Tower height 145 m minus the assumed 20 m mount height.

physics.t_base_at_tower_top_s.est: Computed by the liftoff model (src/physics/liftoff.ts) for 5,400 t and 125 m of rise; 6.7-7.3 s over the mass range (7.4 s if the deck were at ground level).

physics.v_base_at_tower_top_mps.est: Computed by the liftoff model at that time.

physics.a_net_at_tower_top_mps2.est: Computed by the liftoff model; proper acceleration there is 1.58 g.

physics.photo_time_estimate_s.est: booster base ~10-15 m above tower top in reference image, by eye

physics.max_q_time_f14_s.src: https://www.spacelaunchschedule.com/launch/starship-starlink-group-31-1-starship-flight-14/ (Max-Q at T+58 s, MECO T+2:20, stage separation T+2:22; the Wikipedia flight page gives no max-Q time, and live blogs say "about T+1 min")

physics.meco_time_f14_s.src: https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/09/28/starship-returns-to-earth-rocket-splashes-down-north-of-hawaii-after-three-hour-flight/ ("Two minutes and 20 seconds after liftoff, the rest of the first stage engines began shutting down"); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starship_flight_test_14 (MECO and hot staging about T+2:20)

physics.max_q_model_kPa.est: Peak dynamic pressure of this app's vertical-only liftoff model (src/physics/liftoff.ts), about 25 kPa near T+45 s. It has no gravity turn and uses a placeholder throttle-down, so it is an order-of-magnitude guide, not a Starship figure.

physics.meco_alt_est_km.est: Estimate from this app's ascent model (about 55 km) and range 55-70 km; no published altitude at staging was found.

physics.meco_speed_est_mps.est: Estimate from this app's ascent model, range about 1.6-1.8 km/s; no published speed at staging was found.

physics.deluge_water_pad1_gal.src: https://www.faa.gov/media/72826 (FAA Written Re-evaluation of the 2022 PEA: a maximum of about 358,000 gallons; earlier documents and news say 350,000, e.g. https://interestingengineering.com/innovation/spacex-starship-water-deluge-system). This is the Pad 1 design figure; Pad 2 filings allow more.

physics.deluge_water_pad1_kg.est: 358,000 US gal x 3.785 L/gal x 1 kg/L.

physics.deluge_vaporised_fraction.src: https://www.faa.gov/media/72826 (SpaceX estimates 92 % of the 358,000 gallons is vaporised; quoted in search excerpts of the FAA document, the PDF itself was not fetchable)

physics.deluge_pad2_test_flow_gpm.src: https://www.basenor.com/blogs/news/spacex-tests-starship-pad-2-flame-deflector-at-650-000-gpm (a 10 July 2026 test, citing a third-party post on X; unconfirmed, low reliability)

physics.deluge_pad2_test_flow_m3ps.est: 650,000 US gal/min x 3.785e-3 m3/gal / 60 s = 41 m3/s, from the unconfirmed report above.

physics.deluge_vaporisation_energy_J.est: Vaporised water 0.92 x 1.355e6 kg x 2.6 MJ/kg (heating from 25 C to 100 C plus latent heat 2.26 MJ/kg).

physics.combustion_h2o_tps.est: Upper bound: 19.5 t/s of oxygen fully burning methane (CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O) gives 19.5 x 36/64 = 11 t/s of water. Fuel-rich exhaust makes less until it mixes with air.

physics.combustion_co2_tps.est: Upper bound: 19.5 t/s of oxygen x 44/64 = 13.4 t/s of carbon dioxide, if all carbon ends as CO2.

physics.sound_speed_25C_mps.est: 331.3 x sqrt(1 + 25/273.15) = 346 m/s. The 25 C morning air temperature at launch is assumed, not measured.

physics.acoustic_eff_central.est: 0.5 % chosen inside the 0.2-0.8 % range of NASA SP-8072 (https://ntrs.nasa.gov/archive/nasa/casi.ntrs.nasa.gov/19710023719.pdf); an empirical rule of thumb, not a Starship measurement.

physics.sound_power_level_dB.est: 10 log10(0.005 x 1.31e11 W / 1e-12 W) = 208 dB re 1 pW; range 204-210 dB for 0.2-0.8 % efficiency.

physics.spl_100m_dB.est: Sound power level minus 20 log10(100 m) minus 8 (hemispherical free-field spreading), no deluge or shielding. Overpredicts the far field.

physics.spl_1km_dB.est: Same free-field spreading model at 1 km.

physics.spl_10km_measured_dB.src: https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jel/article/4/11/113601/3320807/Starship-super-heavy-acoustics-Far-field-noise (Gee et al., JASA Express Letters 4, 113601, Nov 2024: Flight 5, Oct 2024, far-field 9.7-35.5 km); about 105 dB at Port Isabel, ~10 km, via https://old-man-par.com/2024/12/11/starship-measured-at-ten-times-falcon-9-sound-level/ (which does not state the exact metric, taken here as maximum SPL)

physics.spl_20km_measured_dB.src: https://old-man-par.com/2024/12/11/starship-measured-at-ten-times-falcon-9-sound-level/ (about 90 dB at Laguna Vista, ~20 km, Flight 5 far-field measurements; https://pubs.aip.org/asa/jel/article/4/11/113601/3320807/Starship-super-heavy-acoustics-Far-field-noise)

physics.near_field_dB.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sound_suppression_system (general launch-pad statement: "noise levels approaching 200 dB"; not a Starship measurement)

physics.faa_lmax_contour_dB.src: https://www.faa.gov/media/72826 via search summary; contour within Starbase property

physics.sound_front_radius_at_photo_m.est: c x (T_freeze + 3 s) = 346 m/s x (7.2 + 3) s from the ignition sound, from the liftoff model.

physics.plume_radiant_flux_100m_kWm2.est: Order-of-magnitude estimate only, no published measurement: emissivity 0.2 x sigma T^4 at 2,500 K (2.2 MW/m2) x view factor 0.1 = about 40 kW/m2; ignores steam and atmospheric absorption.

physics.plume_radiant_flux_1km_kWm2.est: Inverse-square scaling of the 100 m estimate (x 1/100).

physics.raptor_exit_mach.est: Isentropic estimate, gamma 1.2, expansion ratio 34.3 (assumed from Raptor 1).

vehicle.raptor3.thrust_sl.src: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SpaceX_Raptor ; consistent with 80.8 MN total (33 x 250 tf). 280 tf press figure rejected (see physics.md)

scene.sun_altitude.est: Computed solar position (low-precision almanac) for lat 25.9968, lon -97.15804 at 2026-09-28 12:48:59 UTC: alt 5.73 deg, az 95.2 deg. Researcher values of 8 and 19 deg rejected.

scene.vehicle_base_height.est: Photo: booster base row 441 vs tower top row 465 (tower 144.5 m) with camera 105 m up at ~705 m: atan geometry gives ~158 m. R2 got 160, R1 got 140 (assumed a lower camera).

scene.t_freeze.est: Liftoff model: engine plane climbs from the mount deck (20 m, est) to 158 m at about T+7.2 s for 5,400 t and 80.8 MN (7.0-7.8 s for 5,300-5,700 t). The physics module recomputes it and a test checks it.

scene.camera.pos.est: research/camera-estimate.md, OSM overlay reprojection within 20-30 px

scene.camera.vfov.est: f = 1133 px on a 943 px tall frame -> 2*atan(471.5/1133). HFOV 73 deg. +-25% (trades off against distance).

scene.olm_deck_height.est: No published figure found; 20 m is a low-confidence estimate (range 15-25 m); it sets the vehicle rest height and the mount model.

scene.trench_axis.src: OSM way tagged construction:aeroway=flame_trench (about 84 x 18 m, rotated about 33 deg, the same rotation as the tower footprints); consistent with the symmetric left/right cloud banks in the photo (camera right = bearing 116.8 deg)

scene.volume_bounds_min.est: Launch-cloud domain enclosing both photo cloud masses (E and W along the trench axis) plus the rising billows

scene.volume_bounds_max.est: z raised to 420 so the ground roll in front of the east bank can reach toward the camera (volume builder request)

scene.vehicle_tilt.est: Photo: nose tip x=826 vs engine plane x=818 over 208 px, with the camera roll at 0.2 deg. The stack leans about 2.2 deg toward the camera's right (ESE), away from the tower.

scene.trench_yaw.src: atan2(0.546, 0.838) from the OSM trench polygon; rotation.y = -33.1 deg maps local +x onto the trench axis

physics.liftoff_thrust_f14_report_Mlbf.src: https://spaceflightnow.com/2026/09/28/starship-returns-to-earth-rocket-splashes-down-north-of-hawaii-after-three-hour-flight/ ("some 16 million pounds of thrust"; a rounded news figure that does not match 33 x 250 tf = 18.2 Mlbf and was not reconciled)
